cohort: All deliveries at the National Maternity Hospital, Dublin, Ireland, between 1940 and 2009
finding: The incidence of umbilical cord prolapse has significantly decreased over the 69-year period, while perinatal survival has increased, likely due to the increased use of caesarean section as the standard delivery method for this emergency.
mod_finding: The increased use of caesarean section for umbilical cord prolapse is likely a major factor in the observed reduction in perinatal mortality.
